newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols retreat from highs in U.S..
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols retreat from highs in U.S..

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark options were off early highs in choppy U.S. trading as the spot dollar pulled back from a 94-month peak of 1.8730 marks touched overnight, dealers said.
Volatilities, particularly the shorter maturities, had become very sensitive to spot movements in either direction, said Ted Voorhees, a senior trader at Deutsche Bank.

"When the dollar breaks higher, everyone scrambles for options. There seems to be no risk appetite whatsoever in the front end," he said. "And then when spot comes off a little bit, they're quickest to hit the front end."
Shorter dated options have higher gamma, which provides quicker premium acceleration and bigger delta swings against spot movement, but also have steeper time decay.
While the relatively slow, steady pace of the dollar's advance in recent weeks has been keeping the front end vulnerable to time decay, the back end was more resilient against the dollar's pullbacks.
Traders said that was because of end-user purchases which had made many bank dealers short in those maturities.
"People who sell them are constantly on the bid because they don't want to be short vega," Voorhees said.
Longer-dated options have higher vega, the rate of change in premiums per change in implied volatility levels.

"There seems to be a lot of buying in the back dates," noted an interbank broker in New York. "We see some selling but it comes back bid. So I would say that we won't see very much softer levels for now."
One-month dollar/mark implied volatility stood at 10.5/10.7 perecnt in early afternoon U.S. business, down half a point from early highs. It was at 10.4/10.7 late on Friday.
One-year was pegged at 10.9/11.1 percent, off 0.1 point from earlier in the day but up a few tenths from Friday.

Dollar/Swiss franc volatilities were also under pressure due to the spot's movement largely in tandem with dollar/mark. Spot hit a four-year high of 1.5356 francs early on but has since come off below 1.5300.
One-month dollar/Swiss was put at 0.1/0.3 point above one-month dollar/mark. The spread in recent years had usually been more than a full point until the dollar's rally in the past few months.
In the one-week area, dollar/Swiss volatilities were below dollar/mark.
Dollar/yen volatilities were also off highs but steadier as the dollar drifted in the mid-118-yen area, slightly below Friday's 119.17 yen high.
One-month dollar/yen was quoted at 11.3/11.5 perecnt, off a few tenths of a point from early highs but up a few tenths but up marginally from late Friday levels.
One-year dollar/yen was also a touch higher at 12.0/12.2 percent.
